how: the conclusion: 'frame D1's one undetermined Higgs bit is the tick's own orientation; an odd number of ticks flips it, an even number keeps it; it is not a free input'. ON MAIN: the tick flips the pair and its square, the act, keeps it. ALSO ON MAIN, and not in the card: the bit is flipped as well by a unitary that the object has for itself, S6, which inverts the act (record sm-c19-01). So the bit is the bundle's orientation, of which the tick's is one factor; and the link to the even-tick condition holds as far as histories are counted by ticks with the act's direction fixed
note: ADDED 2026-11-18: the physical lane's finding C8-02, checked on main: the ground space is a complex plane and every unit vector of it is a ground direction of the quadratic problem; 'one bit' presumes the restriction to the two eigenlines, which no computation on the record forces (record physical-c8-01).
